source: Gyurme Dorje 2001 White Beryl Part VII, printed pp262–280/PDF263–281, chapters f428a–435b

source_notes.paraphrase: The impact-of-hour chapter allows queries at daybreak, sunrise, morning, noon, early afternoon, late afternoon and sunset, with distinct traditional portents; it recommends no divinations after sunset or before daybreak.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The introduction notes separate divination procedures using 7,770 or 1,554 pebbles for past, present or future circumstances; these figures refer to different calculation complexities, not observed prediction samples.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Plate 20 fig.6 catalogues separate adverse narratives for all seven permitted consultation dayparts, spanning household disputes, lost resources and culturally interpreted spirit afflictions.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Plates9 fig18 and 10 fig4 classify the hour's destiny element Wood/Fire/Earth/Iron/Water, with separate columns for subject's class, children, spouse, parents, neighbors, livestock, property and land.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The Wood-hour destiny-element row asserts partly favorable family status but also alleges child survival and other outcomes; such descriptions are query-time claims, not birth-only personality outcomes.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Plate21 fig2 presents a different profile per trigram controlling the hour, including architectural directions, colors, objects and alleged causes of interruption. This is separate from elemental destiny-hour rows.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: White Beryl ff.430a–435b describes a further nine numeric-square system controlling the consultation hour and classifying people, property, spirits and shapes; the chart must not be read as a natal mewa alone.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: A body-grid divination sets the subject lying on their back with head facing west and projects numeric-square sectors onto specific body parts, used for family-relative and life-stage prognoses.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: In the three-generations numeric-square method the day's mewa occupies the chart center, the remaining eight sequentially occupy E,SE,S,SW,W,NW,N,NE, and each position is compared to the year or day's square.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The east sector is read for father, grandfather, great-grandfather; outcomes differ when the sector's element inhibits the annual one versus the reverse directed relation.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The southeast sector is read for mother, grandmother, great-grandmother, and the source explicitly contrasts the sector mewa with the day's square, not always the year's square.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Plate21 fig4 allocates nine named adverse symbolic sectors to each mewa, from paternal loss of homeland and widowhood to divorce, household conflict and prosperity for livestock; these are historical associations not independent real cases.
source_notes.status: English commentary/translated source claim, not original Tibetan collation

key_distinction: Consultation-hour fate is not a natal birth-hour prediction and contains observational/ritual side inputs.
